area_title: Concrete filter examples plus lower addendum / middleware-before-filters reminder
what_area_is_about: concrete ASP.NET Core MVC filter examples: authorization, resource, action, exception, result and endpoint filters
where each filter type can short-circuit, access context, run before/after next, or shape results
resource-filter caching and the important fact that it can run before model binding/action execution
always-run result filters and result-wrapping behavior
endpoint filters for minimal APIs / endpoint routing and their per-endpoint argument/result pipeline
lower addendum that contrasts middleware, global MVC filters, controller/action filters and endpoint filters
key_ideas: Authorization filters are for early request gating and should not be treated as catch-all exception/result handlers.
Resource filters can short-circuit before model binding and action invocation, which makes them useful for cached responses and broad MVC wrapping.
Action filters wrap action execution and are a natural place for timing/logging around an action method.
Exception filters can convert handled MVC exceptions into results, but the earlier R01 caveats still apply.
Result filters wrap result execution; always-run result filters exist for cases where normal result filters may be skipped by earlier short-circuiting.
Endpoint filters are endpoint/minimal-API focused and can inspect arguments/results around `next`, while MVC filters apply inside MVC action/result execution.
Middleware runs before MVC filters; non-MVC requests may never enter MVC filters at all.
